# Skip `/slots` polls for definitively unloaded models

**Parent:** LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K · **Slice:** 3 of 5 · **Type:** feature · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

Put the unloaded-model guard in the single shared `/slots` resolution path
(`_resolve_local_slots_target()`, plan Q1 = A) and make **every**
proxy-initiated `/slots` call site honour the resulting skip: no router
request, no `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` increment, no
`slots_child_port_unavailable` warning for a model the router definitively
reports as not loaded — while a *loaded* model with no discoverable child port
keeps producing the genuine signal.

## Why this slice

This is the tracer bullet for the parent defect: the chat dispatch for
`gpt120` (2026-10-28T10:45:00.404Z) currently polls the router, takes a 400 and
records a fallback, so a real child-port discovery regression is
indistinguishable from unloaded-model noise (parent AC1/AC2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Unloaded model is not counted.** A `/slots` poll for a model that
      is not currently loaded does **not** increment
      `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
      and emits no `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning (asserted via the
      counter/warning in a test; the router is not contacted).
- [ ] **AC2 — Loaded-model regression still pinned.** A `/slots` poll for the
      loaded chat model whose child port cannot be discovered **still**
      increments the counter and emits the throttled warning (regression test,
      must fail if the guard swallows loaded-model discovery failures).
- [ ] **AC3 — `/status` capacity truth preserved.** `/status` continues to
      report truthful capacity (existing "definitive model absent" behaviour:
      fail-open on the configured pool, no resurrected fossil counts).
- [ ] **AC6 — Skip is observable.** The `/metrics` counter (implemented here as
      `llama_slots_child_port_skipped_total{reason="model_not_loaded"}`, with a
      throttled debug log line naming the skipped model) makes a skipped poll
      distinguishable from a poll that was never attempted, so AC1 can be
      verified post-deploy; registered in `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` with a
      docstring in the style of `record_slots_child_port_fallback()`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Admission outcome unchanged.** A test pins that skipping the
      availability check for an unloaded model returns the same admission
      result (`None`) as the current definitive-400 fall-through — the fix must
      not start refusing or blocking requests.
- [ ] **Fail open.** When the loaded-set answer is indeterminate (`None`) the
      poll proceeds exactly as today (test: probe error ⇒ `/slots` still
      issued, counter increment on discovery failure unchanged).
- [ ] **Every call site honours the skip** (Q1 = A): `_check_slot_availability()`
      and `poll_slots_for_model()` (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`), the `/status`
      handler slots path (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`), the SSE broadcast loop
      (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) and the SSE initial payload
      (`proxy/proxy/ui.py`) issue **no** `/slots` request when the resolver
      reports a skip — asserted per call site.
- [ ] The resolver's skip sentinel is documented in its docstring and the
      shared call-site test is extended so a future call site that ignores the
      sentinel fails the suite.
- [ ] Slice 1's AC2 pin tests in `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py`
      stay green **unchanged** (extended with AC1/AC6/AC7 cases, never weakened
      or deleted) — the guard must not swallow the loaded-model signal.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the
      change (run through the test skill; changed-scope gate first).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `_resolve_local_slots_target()` to consult
  `is_model_known_unloaded()` (slice 2) **before** discovery, returning a
  documented skip sentinel (e.g. `(None, None)`) when the model is definitively
  not loaded; keep `_warn_child_port_fallback()` on the loaded-model path
  untouched (AC2).
- Emit the skip signal once per skip: `record_slots_child_port_skipped("model_not_loaded")`
  plus a throttled debug log.
- Teach the five call sites to return early on the sentinel, preserving each
  one's existing fallback behaviour when no skip is reported.
- New focused suite `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py` for
  AC1/AC2/AC6/AC7/fail-open/call-site coverage; extend
  `proxy/tests/test_slots_query_target_call_sites.py` with the sentinel
  contract.
- Update the `_resolve_local_slots_target()` docstring's rule list with the
  skip case.
- Verify `proxy/tests/test_slot_availability_dedicated_client.py` and
  `proxy/tests/test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — guard in `_resolve_local_slots_target()`, skip sentinel, docstring
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `llama_slots_child_port_skipped_total` + recorder

# Router startup pins `current_model` to `router_preload_list[0]`, which can be a non-chat preset

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K (`discovered-from:LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K`) · **Type:** bug · **Priority:** medium

## Problem

In router mode the proxy sets `srv.current_model` to the **first** preload entry
at startup (`proxy/proxy/server.py`, `if resolved: current_model = resolved[0]`
in the router-preload branch), which can be a non-chat preset such as
`mxbai-embed`. `srv.current_model` is only replaced by the loaded llama model
name once a chat dispatch resolves it (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`, router-mode
`current_model` assignment).

Consequences while the pinned value persists:

- The proxy believes a non-chat model is current, so model-scoped paths that
  default to `srv.current_model` (slot polling, `/status` capacity reporting,
  SSE per-slot detail) query the embed child rather than the chat child.
- `/slots` resolution for the pinned name can legitimately fail child-port
  discovery, which produces the **genuine** `slots_child_port_unavailable`
  fallback signal for a loaded model — the live example is the
  `model=mxbai-embed` warning at `2026-10-31T00:42:00.198Z` on proxy pid
  3944027. That is the AC2 shape LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K must keep counting, so it
  is *correct* to keep counting it here as well; the defect is the bookkeeping
  that makes the embed preset "current" at all.

## Why this is a separate item

LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K (unloaded-model `/slots` skip) deliberately does **not**
trust `srv.current_model` as proof of loadedness and explicitly records this
startup behaviour as out of scope ("Scope-creep risk: the startup
`current_model = router_preload_list[0]` behaviour ... is a *separate* defect
about loaded-model bookkeeping. Record as a linked follow-up rather than
widening this item").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The startup preload path no longer selects a non-chat preset as
      `current_model`: the value is chosen from the router's `/models` loaded
      set with a documented preference rule (chat model first), or left unset
      until the first dispatch resolves it — decision recorded in the item.
- [ ] A test pins that a preload list whose first entry is a non-chat preset
      (e.g. `mxbai-embed`) does **not** leave that preset as
      `srv.current_model` after startup in router mode.
- [ ] Model-scoped slot/capacity paths are asserted to target the chat child
      after startup, not the first-spawned child.
- [ ] The genuine loaded-model-without-child-port fallback signal still fires
      when it should (no weakening of LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3 or
      LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K AC2).
- [ ] Changed-scope test gate green through the test skill.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — router-preload branch that sets `current_model`
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — router-mode `current_model` assignment and `router_list_models()`
- `proxy/tests/` — startup preload / current-model regression test

## Related work

- **LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K** — unloaded-model `/slots` skip (this defect is its
  documented follow-up).
- **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — `/models`-derived model id resolution (the source of
  the loaded set this item would prefer).
- **LP-0MTP1FQXH004JYEF** — model-filtered child-port discovery (`mxbai-embed`
  vs `Qwen3`): the reason a model name is passed to discovery at all.
- **LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1** — reporting configured slot capacity when no model is
  loaded.

## Out of scope

- The unloaded-model skip itself (LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K).
- Changing router preload ordering or eviction policy.

# Pin the loaded-model child-port fallback signal (AC2 baseline, green)

**Parent:** LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K · **Slice:** 1 of 5 · **Type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Summary

Write the **test-first** pins for the signal the unloaded-model guard must not
swallow: a `/slots` poll for a **loaded** model whose child port cannot be
discovered still increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}` and
emits the throttled `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning. The tests are green
against today's code (they are characterisation pins), so they must stay green
after the guard lands — that is what makes the future guard safe.

## Why this slice

LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3 was built because the discovery helper once swallowed
failures silently for weeks; the parent's biggest risk is a guard that
"helpfully" also suppresses the genuine loaded-model regression. Pinning the
signal **before** changing the resolver means any accidental suppression fails
the suite immediately, and the parent's AC2 has an independent owner rather than
living only inside the change that could break it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py` pins: a `/slots` poll for a
      model the router's `/models` reports as **loaded**, with no discoverable
      child port, increments
      `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
      exactly once and emits the throttled `slots_child_port_unavailable`
      warning naming that model.
- [ ] The same module pins single-server mode (`llama_router_mode: false`): the
      fallback is counted under `no_child_port_single_server` and logged at
      debug level only — unchanged by this parent's work.
- [ ] The same module pins **fail-open characterisation**: when loadedness is
      *indeterminate* (the `/models` probe errors, returns non-200, or the model
      name is absent/unresolvable), today's behaviour — poll the resolved
      target and count a discovery fallback — is asserted, so the guard cannot
      turn an unknown answer into a skip.
- [ ] Tests are green on the current tree and are written so they remain valid
      after the guard lands (assertions on counters/warnings/requests, not on
      internal call order), so they become the AC2 regression pin.
- [ ] No production code changes in this slice; changed-scope test gate green
      through the test skill.

discovered-from:LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K

## Problem statement

Several open work items each require a **restart-free 24 h** production window, but a
proxy restart resets the in-process residency/lease state that those windows measure —
and every deploy restarts the proxy. The restarts therefore invalidate *each other's*
windows, and each invalidation costs a full re-arm plus (often) a wasted dispatched
session.

Observed on 2026-10-31 alone, inside the re-arm #3 window
`2026-10-30T10:36:00Z → 2026-10-31T10:36:00Z` of `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K`:

| # | Restart (UTC) | New pid | Attribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-10-30T23:10:49Z | 3797968 | `LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK deploy post-deadline re-dispatch fix (5b35dd80) — 24h measurement anchor` |
| 2 | 2026-10-31T00:37:53Z | 3938219 | `source=manual actor=unknown reason=manual` |
| 3 | 2026-10-31T00:41:57Z | 3944027 | `source=manual actor=unknown reason=manual` |

Restart #1 was another measurement item's own deploy anchor; #2 and #3 were unattributed
manual restarts four minutes apart, which also invalidated that item's freshly armed
`2026-10-30T23:10:47Z → 2026-10-31T23:10:47Z` window.

Open items currently competing for mutually exclusive restart-free windows (at least):

- `LP-0MVN44XB0009M33K` — 24 h AC4 verification of resident-prefix admission (re-arm #4)
- `LP-0MVVJYJQ9001I8QK` — post-deadline re-dispatch fix, >= 24 h post-deploy window
- `LP-0MVVLQMG1000843Q` — writer-side sidecar pairing fix, >= 24 h post-deploy window
- `LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6` — router:500 == 0 over 24 h
- `LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57` — router:500 == 0 over 24 h (earliest 2026-10-27T12:00Z)

## Desired outcome

One restart-free 24 h window serves every open measurement whose code is already loaded
by the running process, instead of one re-arm per item and restart-churn between them.

Candidates (pick at intake):

- **A — measurement calendar (process).** A single "measurement window" record (work item
  or file under `docs/dev/`) listing open 24 h measurement items, their required deploy
  commits, and the current restart-free window; new deploys are batched before a window
  opens, and unattributed `manual` restarts are investigated rather than ignored.
- **B — one shared measurement window per deploy generation.** A deploy-generation id
  written into `proxy.log` at `Logging initialised` (it already carries `pid=`), so each
  measurement can state the generation it measured and one analysis run can serve all
  items whose fixes are in that generation.
- **C — enforce the freeze mechanically.** `scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart` refuses (or
  requires `--force` + a reason that names the measurement items it invalidates) while a
  measurement window is open.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. The open 24 h measurement items and their required deploy commits are enumerated in
  one place, with the restart-free window each one currently expects.
- AC2. The chosen mechanism (A, B or C) is implemented and documented so that a restart
  during an open window either serves every waiting item or is visibly refused/recorded as
  invalidating named items.
- AC3. The two unattributed `manual` restarts of 2026-10-31T00:37:53Z / 00:41:57Z are
  attributed to a cause (operator action, tooling, or incident) and recorded.

## Constraints

- Read-only with respect to the proxy's scheduling behaviour; no knob re-tuning.
- Must not weaken the existing AC2 rule on the measurement items: a restart inside a
  window still invalidates that window (this item reduces the *frequency*, it does not
  license measuring across a restart).
data.title: Coordinate restart-free 24 h measurement windows across concurrent verification items (deploys/restarts invalidate each other's windows)

data.description:
## Goal

**As an** operator running unattended workers against this proxy,
**I want** the proxy to recognise when a model's whole provider chain is blocked by
*scheduled* gates it already knows the expiry of (`available_times` windows,
usage-limit resets, quota quarantines) rather than by transient failure,
**so that** the client receives a single meaningful, retryable error that says
*what* is unavailable, *when* it comes back, and *not to retry until then* —
instead of the opaque `503 All providers exhausted` it gets today, which it
retries every ~60 s for hours.

discovered-from:LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135, discovered-from:LP-0MVR7IN0O000DPXN.
Operator decision 2026-10-31: we deliberately do **not** want to add an always-on
remote provider to paper over the gaps — during the scheduled windows some
requests *must* be deferred. This item makes that deferral honest and actionable
rather than appearing as a failure.

## Observed behaviour today (2026-10-31, `model=plan`)

For `model=plan` there is **no eligible remote provider between 06:00 and 10:00
UTC**: `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2` and `opencode-go-3` all carry
`available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`
(`proxy/config.yaml:516, 574, 632`), `munitoai-free` is
`usage_limit_reset_pending` until `2026-11-01T00:02:00Z`, and
`OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` is `quota_exhausted` with `resets_in` ≈ 17 days. So local
(`local-qwen3`) is the only candidate, and every refusal in that window is a hard
failure for the client:

```
08:16:32 Skipping provider=munitoai-free: usage_limit_reset_pending
         (reset_at=2026-11-01T00:02:00Z, reset_in=56727s)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: quota_exhausted
         (effective_headroom=0.0%, resets_in=1475316s)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
08:16:32 Skipping provider=opencode-go:   outside its available_times window (UTC)
08:16:32 All providers exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions;
         unavailable={'local-qwen3': 59, 'munitoai-free': 56727,
                      'opencode-go-3': 1475436}
08:16:32 Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted
         message for model=v1/chat/completions (status=503)
```

The victim session (`herdr-1793416360-4155786-6690`, pinned) accumulated **113
refusals** and 10 hard `503`s over 7 h 47 m, and one recurrence produced
`~30` further failures between 06:02 and 09:19 — always the same sentence, never
any indication that the earliest possible recovery was the 10:00 UTC window edge.

### Why the two existing mechanisms do not cover this

1. **`_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (`provider.py:6247`) is
   sole-cause-only.** It returns `None` unless *every* recorded attempt is
   `status == "outside_time_window"` (`provider.py:6275-6288`). In the real
   06:00-10:00 case the diagnostics also carry `usage_limit_reset` /
   `quota_exhausted`, so the window-specific body never fires and the client
   falls through to the generic `all_exhausted` 503. The mixed-but-fully-planned
   case — the actual shape of every occurrence — is unhandled.
2. **`_compute_retry_after` (`provider.py:4608`) takes the MAX of its
   candidates** and includes every entry in the process-wide `_usage_reset_at`
   map. In the observed case the maximum is `opencode-go-3`'s 1 475 436 s
   (17 days), so the advertised wait is then clamped to
   `server.max_retry_after_seconds: 3600` (`config.yaml:1261`). The timer the
   client sees is therefore an artefact of the cap, not the real recovery
   instant: the honest answer was the 10:00 UTC window edge (≈ 3 h 44 m away),
   and for a `munitoai-free`-only case at 08:16 it was 16 h away while the client
   was told 3600 s.

Net effect: no `code`, `detail`, or `retry_at` distinguishes *"the fleet is
scheduled off and returns at 10:00 UTC"* from *"everything failed just now"*.
Both are `503 all_exhausted` with a cap-derived `Retry-After`.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (classification).** A new classifier separates a chain blocked
  **exclusively** by *known-until* gates from one blocked by *transient*
  failure. Known-until gate statuses are exactly: `outside_time_window`,
  `usage_limit_reset` (the reset instant is known), `quota_exhausted` (the reset
  interval is known) and `provider_budget_exhausted` (window rollover is known).
  Transient/unknown statuses are: `connection_error`, `http_error` / `HTTP <n>`,
  `empty_response`, `stream_error`, `stream_reroute`, `local_admission_reject`,
  and anything unrecognised. The new response applies **only** when every
  attempt is known-until and at least one provider was window- or reset-blocked;
  a single transient attempt keeps today's behaviour byte-identically.
- **AC2 (honest recovery instant).** The response advertises the **earliest**
  instant *any* entry in the chain becomes eligible — the minimum over window
  edges and known resets — not the maximum. Unit rows:
  (a) the 2026-10-31 08:16 chain ⇒ `retry_at` is the next `10:00` UTC window
  edge, not `now + 3600 s`, and not the 17-day quota reset;
  (b) `munitoai-free`-only at 08:16 (reset `2026-11-01T00:02Z`) ⇒ `retry_at` is
  that reset instant;
  (c) a chain whose earliest recovery is already past ⇒ treated as available now
  (fail-open; today's behaviour, never a stale `retry_at`).
- **AC3 (cap is honest, never silent).** `Retry-After` equals the body
  `retry_after`, as every other refusal does. When the true wait exceeds
  `server.max_retry_after_seconds`, the advertised `retry_after` is capped **and**
  the body carries the untruncated `retry_at` plus an explicit truncation flag
  (e.g. `retry_after_truncated: true`), so a client can choose to sleep through
  the window instead of polling every hour. No silent cap.
- **AC4 (stable discriminator, back-compatible).** The response carries a new
  stable `code` (e.g. `no_provider_available_in_window`) plus `retryable: true`,
  and a `detail` naming the earliest reopening provider and its gate. The
  existing prose `error` field keeps a value that older clients already
  understand (today's `All providers exhausted`), so no existing client
  string-match breaks. `EXHAUSTION_CODE_TIME_WINDOW`'s existing sole-cause
  behaviour is preserved exactly.
- **AC5 (no regression).** The sole-cause window response and the generic
  `all_exhausted` / `all_slots_exhausted` / `local_admission_reject` responses
  are unchanged for their existing triggers; their contract suites
  (`proxy/tests/test_admission_refusal_retry_contract.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`) pass unmodified.
- **AC6 (observability — one line an operator can act on).** One log line at the
  chain end names every blocked entry, its gate class and the instant it
  reopens, plus the aggregate `retry_at`, so the condition is diagnosable without
  joining skip lines:
  `chain_planned_unavailable model=plan retry_at=2026-10-31T10:00:00Z blocked=[opencode-go:window@10:00Z, opencode-go-2:window@10:00Z, opencode-go-3:quota@<iso>, munitoai-free:usage_reset@<iso>]`.
  One line per request, not per entry, and no new per-provider vocabulary.
- **AC7 (pinned clients get this too).** A `local-preferred` request whose local
  route is refused inside a known-until window receives this response (or an
  equivalent that carries the same `retry_at`/`code`), rather than a bare
  `429 Local admission refused` with an unrelated local-capacity timer. The
  incident shape (`X-Local-Preference: local-preferred`, local refused, remote
  all window/quota blocked, 08:16 UTC) asserts the client is told `10:00Z`.
- **AC8 (fail-open).** Any unparseable window, missing reset instant, unknown
  gate status, or internal exception resolves to today's generic exhausted
  response — never to a fabricated `retry_at`. A provider with no computable
  reopening instant disqualifies the classification (falls back), it is not
  guessed.
- **AC9 (no chain-hold regression).** The chain-hold/wrapper that replays cycles
  still bounds itself by the real wait and does not spin: replaying a
  known-until-exhausted chain must not schedule its next cycle earlier than the
  advertised `retry_at` (bounded by the existing hold caps), asserted in the
  overnight-exhaustion end-to-end suite.
- **AC10 (docs).** `proxy/docs/routing.md` and the `available_times` comment
  block in `proxy/config.yaml` document the classification, the earliest-instant
  rule, the truncation flag, and the operator decision that scheduled gaps are
  deferred-and-reported rather than papered over with a permanent remote
  provider.

## Out of scope

- Adding or re-timing any provider's `available_times` so the gaps disappear —
  explicitly rejected by the operator on 2026-10-31.
- Making a pinned client fall through to remote, or capping how many refusals it
  may accumulate (`LP-0MVUH9PL0005PW90`).
- The measured-cache abort / thrash cooldown (`LP-0MVWBD91Z004U135`,
  `LP-0MVWC8JCG007GAPW`).
- The body/header surface owned by `LP-0MVSS435600370D6` (capacity verdict on the
  admission-reject payload) — this item must compose with it, not replace it.

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` (:6126),
  `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (:6247, the sole-cause gate at
  :6275-6288), `_compute_retry_after` (:4608), `_refusal_retry_timing` (:4830),
  `_budget_window_retry_after` (:4660), `_seconds_until_next_window`,
  `_record_quarantine_attempts`, `_providers_outside_window`,
  `EXHAUSTION_CODE_*` (:6006-6010), the chain-end call sites (:12236, :14535).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — canonical reason vocabulary (:113).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `max_retry_after_seconds` (:1261), the `available_times`
  comment block (:505-516).
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_refusal_retry_contract.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_overnight_exhaustion_e2e.py`.

## Assumptions

- Window edges and usage-limit resets are the *only* known-until gates whose
  expiry this proxy can compute reliably; anything else must fail open (AC8).
- Advertising a long `retry_at` (hours) is safe for existing clients: they either
  honour `Retry-After` (bounded by the existing cap) or ignore it as today.
- The earliest-instant rule is the right semantics for a *client* even though the
  chain-hold wrapper benefits from the conservative maximum; the two are kept
  separate (AC9), not merged into one number.

## Goal

**As** an operator running pinned `local-preferred` workers, **I want**
`decide_measured_cache_abort()` to abort only when the measured cold prefill
genuinely cannot complete inside the request's own prefill-deadline budget,
**so that** a mid-size prompt that fits the budget is never cancelled into a
600 s thrash cooldown and an endless `429 Local admission refused` loop.

Parent AC1, AC5 (continue detail), AC6, AC10. **Test-first**: the decision rows
item is written first and this item turns it green.

## Scope

Add a third, **benefit** gate to the decision, evaluated *after* the existing
ratio floor and token bound (both keep their current semantics):

1. price the **measured** deficit `measured_new = total - cache` with
   `proxy.prefill_eta.estimate_prefill_seconds(model, measured_new,
   cached_ratio=0.0, config=...)` — the same call the admission guard makes,
   including its configured conservative p75 uplift for prompts ≥
   `local_admission_guard_eta_percentile_min_tokens` (D3 (a)). Never price it
   from the admission-priced `new_tokens`;
2. compare that ETA against the comparator budget
   `budget_safety_fraction × local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (114 s shipped),
   falling back to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` when the fraction is `0`
   (D1 (a)). The admission wait budget (`budget_seconds`, 60 s) is **not** the
   comparator;
3. `abort=True` only when `measured_eta_s > budget_s`; otherwise `abort=False`
   with `detail="within_eta_budget"` (D2 (a) — no extra margin test beyond the
   comparator's own 5 % safety fraction).

`AbortSettings` gains the gate's inputs — `model`, `config`/resolved budget and
an injectable ETA estimator for deterministic tests — and keeps its fail-open
construction: an unreadable deadline, fraction or estimator resolves to
*continue*, never to a more aggressive abort. `AbortDecision` gains
`measured_eta_s`, `budget_s` and the rate basis so the dispatch log line can
report why a deficit was tolerated (parent AC5). Budget resolution lives in
`proxy.prefill_eta` behind a small public helper wrapping
`_deadline_budget_seconds`, so the advertised threshold can never drift from
the enforced one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — parent AC1 restated (benefit gate: abort only when waiting cannot
  succeed).** The abort decision prices the measured deficit with the same
  calibrated prefill rate model the admission gate uses
  (`proxy.prefill_eta.estimate_prefill_seconds`) and aborts **only when that ETA
  exceeds the request's local prefill budget** — the prefill-deadline budget
  `budget_safety_fraction × local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (114 s shipped),
  falling back to `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120 s) when the fraction is
  `0`. The admission wait budget `budget_seconds` is **not** the comparator, and
  the ETA is priced from the **measured** `total - cache`, never from the
  admission-priced `new_tokens`. Enforced order: ratio floor → token bound →
  ETA budget, so an abort requires all three.
- **AC1b — vocabulary.** `DETAIL_WITHIN_ETA_BUDGET = "within_eta_budget"` is
  added alongside the existing `detail` values — one new `detail` token, no new
  reason token, no new response header, no refusal-body change.
- **AC2 — the pinned rows are green.** The incident row (`total=14380
  cache=0`) continues with `within_eta_budget`; the 56 000-token row still
  aborts with `deficit_over_bound`; the AC10 provenance row shows
  `measured_eta_s >= 30` and never ≈8 s.
- **AC3 — comparator resolution is single-sourced.** A public
  `prefill_eta` helper wraps `_deadline_budget_seconds` (fraction × deadline,
  `0` ⇒ fall back to the deadline); the admission wait budget
  (`budget_seconds` / `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) is never consulted by
  the gate.
- **AC4 — ETA provenance.** The ETA is computed from the measured deficit with
  `cached_ratio=0.0` (a deficit is by definition uncached); `priced_new_tokens`
  continues to gate only the token bound and never prices the ETA.
- **AC5 — fail-open (parent AC6).** Missing/partial/non-numeric measurement, an
  unusable priced value, an unreadable or non-positive deadline/fraction, an
  unusable estimator, an unreadable config, or any internal exception all
  resolve to *continue*; `local_measured_cache_abort_enabled: 0` still restores
  pre-change behaviour exactly (no `return_progress` injection, no capture, no
  early release).
- **AC6 — never raises.** `estimate_prefill_seconds` is called inside the
  module's existing `try` so the never-raises contract is preserved even for a
  pathological config or an estimator stub that raises.
- **AC7 — warm path untouched (parent AC2).** `cache ≥ 0.99 × total` still
  returns `below_deficit_ratio_floor` **before** any ETA work; the existing warm
  and replay tests pass unmodified.
- **AC8 — the changed-scope test gate is green** (`/skill:test`, changed
  scope).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` — `decide_measured_cache_abort`,
  `AbortSettings`, `AbortDecision`, the new `within_eta_budget` detail.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `estimate_prefill_seconds` (`~893`),
  `_deadline_budget_seconds` (`~1293`), `resolve_config` (`~398`).
- `proxy/tests/test_measured_prefill_abort_decision.py` — the pinned rows.
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_deadline.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_conservative.py` — existing deadline-budget
  expectations that must stay green.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the decision-rows item. Blocks the wiring item.

## Deliverables

The benefit gate in production code with a fail-open construction, the
`within_eta_budget` detail, the ETA/budget fields on the decision, and the
public comparator-budget helper — all decision rows green.

## Goal

As a drive operator, I want one shared, table-driven classifier that turns a
failing `finish` report into `{kind, step, reason, message}`, so `phase_drive`
can tell a transient infrastructure refusal from a genuine gate failure instead
of treating every failure as a gate failure (parent AC1).

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts through all layers end-to-end — the `finish`
subprocess's structured `steps` payload, `phase_parent._run_finish`'s report,
and the classifier `phase_drive` consumes — with unit tests and the reference
doc's vocabulary table updated in the same slice.

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - Add module-level constants **next to the emitters** (adjacent to
    `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` / `phase_finish`):
    - `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs (the
      allow-list from the parent item's **Assumptions**).
    - `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` — frozenset of `(step, reason)` pairs for the
      known gate failures (`tests: tests_failed`, `build: build_failed`,
      `worktree_placement: *`, `diff: no_changes`, …) — recorded for
      documentation/consistency only; classification of anything not in
      either set is `unknown`.
    - `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS = ("infrastructure", "gate", "unknown")`.
  - Add `classify_finish_failure(finish_report: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]`
    returning `{kind, step, reason, message}`:
    - resolves `(step, reason)` from the report's structured `steps`
      (precedence: `main_checkout_lock` → `main_checkout_guard` →
      `local_dev_fast_forward` → `push` → `build` → `tests` →
      `ancestry_assertion`), never from prose;
    - `kind = "infrastructure"` only for an explicit allow-list hit;
      `"gate"` for an explicit gate-list hit; otherwise `"unknown"`
      (fail-safe: `unknown` is never `infrastructure`);
    - tolerates `None`, `{}` and non-dict input → `kind="unknown"`.
  - `phase_parent._run_finish`: call `_invoke_implement("finish", …, parse_on_failure=True)`
    and **keep the `None` sentinel** — `_run_finish` still returns `None` on
    failure, but records `report["finish_failure"] = classify_finish_failure(parsed)`
    on the parent report before returning.
  - Record a structured `steps` entry for the `finish` failure exits that have
    none today (the `AncestryAssertionError` handler ~6958 and the generic
    `RuntimeError` push/build/commit handlers), so classification never parses
    prose.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — seed the "Drive failure recovery"
  classification vocabulary table (completed in the docs item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. One module-level vocabulary constant, colocated with the emitters,
   enumerates every `(step, reason)` pair the shipped `finish` code can emit;
   a table-driven test asserts the `kind` mapping for each entry.
2. A `(step, reason)` pair that is not listed classifies as `unknown`, never
   `infrastructure` (table-driven test covers the fail-safe direction).
3. `classify_finish_failure(None)`, `classify_finish_failure({})` and a
   non-dict argument each return `kind="unknown"` without raising.
4. `phase_parent._run_finish` invokes `finish` with `parse_on_failure=True`,
   still returns `None` on failure (sentinel pinned by a regression test), and
   the returned parent report carries `finish_failure` with the correct
   `step`/`reason`/`kind` for a scripted failing finish report.
5. Every `finish` failure exit that previously carried no structured `steps`
   entry (ancestry assertion, generic push failure, generic `RuntimeError`)
   records `{success: false, reason}` in `steps`, so no classification path
   depends on `report["message"]` prose.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC1 traceability.** **Single classifier for finish failures.** `phase_drive` classifies each failing `finish` as `infrastructure`, `gate` or `unknown` through one shared, table-driven classifier over an explicit `(step, reason)` vocabulary, derived from the `finish` subprocess report (threaded out of `phase_parent`'s `_run_finish`). Unit test: a table-driven test asserts the mapping for every refusal reason the shipped code can emit, and that an unlisted reason classifies as `unknown` (fail-safe, never `infrastructure`). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the three module-level constants beside `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push`
   and `phase_finish`, with a comment stating the drift rule (a new `_refuse`
   reason must be added to the table in the same commit).
2. Write the failing table-driven test first (`TestFinishFailureClassifier`),
   enumerating the emitted pairs; then implement `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Thread `parse_on_failure=True` through `_run_finish`, keeping the `None`
   sentinel and adding `report["finish_failure"]`; add the sentinel regression
   test.
4. Add the missing structured `steps` entries in `phase_finish`'s failure
   exits; assert them in a test.
5. Seed the reference doc vocabulary table.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `classify_finish_failure` (new),
  `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_GATE_REFUSALS` / `FINISH_FAILURE_KINDS`
  (new), `phase_parent._run_finish` (~7558), `phase_finish` failure handlers
  (~6780–6980), `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` (~3595–3740).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestFinishFailureClassifier`.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — "Drive failure recovery" table.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Vocabulary drift** — a future `_refuse` reason is added and silently
  classifies as `gate`, re-creating the discard hazard. *Mitigation:* the
  constant sits next to the emitters; the table test enumerates every emitted
  pair; `unknown` fails safe.
- **`parse_on_failure=True` alters the placement-guard path.** *Mitigation:*
  the `None` sentinel is kept and pinned by a regression test.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice; every other child consumes
`classify_finish_failure` / `finish_failure`.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC1 (primary) — the single table-driven classifier; supplies the
`finish_failure` evidence payload that AC5's reporting slice consumes.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code
  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

## Goal

As a maintainer writing the recovery tests, I want the drive test harness to
script finish failures **with a step and reason** and to provide a real
in-repo worktree that carries a commit ahead of the parent branch, so the
infra-retry, preservation-gate and gate-regression slices can each be pinned by
a deterministic test without touching production code (parent AC2, AC3, AC6).

Test-first item: it lands before the implementation slices that consume it.

## Scope

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`
  - Extend `finishing_failed_report(child_id, message=None, *, step=None,
    reason=None, kind=None)` so the emitted parent report carries the
    `finish_failure` payload produced by `classify_finish_failure`. Default
    arguments must reproduce today's report shape exactly (backwards
    compatible — existing callers unchanged).
  - Add a `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture: a real git repo with a `dev`
    branch plus a linked worktree whose branch holds one commit `dev` does not
    (and, separately, an uncommitted-only variant reusing the existing
    `child_worktree` fixture).
  - Add a `RecordingReset` / `recording_reset` helper that wraps
    `_reset_child_worktree` and records every call plus the git commands
    observed, so a test can assert "no destructive command ran".
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — only if the harness helpers are shared;
  keep changes additive.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `finishing_failed_report()` accepts `step`/`reason`/`kind` keyword
   arguments and emits a parent report whose `finish_failure` payload drives
   the production classifier to the expected `kind`; called with no extra
   arguments it emits byte-identical keys to today's helper.
2. A `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture creates a real repo + linked worktree
   whose `HEAD` is ahead of `dev`, and a meta-test asserts that setup (the
   ahead-of-parent relationship holds, and the commit is reachable).
3. A meta-test asserts the fixture's worktree is detected as "has changes"
   while a clean worktree at `dev` is not, so a later preservation test cannot
   pass vacuously.
4. A recording helper proves a test can assert that **no** `git reset --hard`
   or `git clean -fd` ran against a given worktree path.
5. `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` and `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
   remain green with the extended harness (no existing test edited to
   accommodate it).
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the harness extension and its meta-tests first (they must fail before
   the production code from the classifier slice is available only where they
   depend on it — this item depends on that slice).
2. Extend `finishing_failed_report` additively, defaulting to the current
   shape.
3. Add the `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture with explicit setup assertions.
4. Add the recording reset helper.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `finishing_failed_report` (~94),
  `DriveHarness` (~141), `child_worktree` fixture (~608).
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — loop-bound / CLI-flag coverage (additive).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Harness edits silently weaken existing assertions.** *Mitigation:* all
  changes additive; existing tests must not be edited (AC5).
- **A fixture that is ahead-of-parent only by accident.** *Mitigation:* the
  meta-test asserts the ancestry relationship explicitly (AC2/AC3).

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading` — supplies
  `classify_finish_failure` and the `finish_failure` report payload this
  harness scripts.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC2, AC3, AC6 — test infrastructure only (no production behaviour
changes); lands before the implementation slices that consume it.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator driving an epic unattended on a contended host, I want a
transient infrastructure refusal (`local_dev_diverged`, main-checkout lock
held, push transport drop) to be retried on its **own** bounded budget with
backoff instead of consuming the finish-attempt budget, so a refusal that
clears seconds later no longer discards a committed slice (parent AC2).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: classify `parent_report["finish_failure"]` on every
    `finishing_failed` report.
    - `kind == "infrastructure"` → increment `infra_retries[child]`, emit a
      `children_driven` entry with `result: "infra-retry"`, sleep the injected
      backoff, `continue` (re-run `parent`, which re-runs `finish`; **never**
      spawn a session). `finish_attempts[child]` is **not** incremented.
    - `kind in {"gate", "unknown"}` → existing bounded path unchanged.
  - New `--infra-retry-limit N` argparse flag (default `5`, non-positive
    clamped to 1) plumbed into `phase_drive` as `infra_retry_limit`.
  - New report keys: `infra_retries` (dict child → count),
    `infra_retry_limit` (int). Existing keys keep their meaning/types.
  - Backoff: `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` → `min(2 * 2**(attempt-1), 30)`
    seconds, with an injectable delay callable (`sleep`/`delay` parameter on
    `phase_drive`, default `time.sleep`) so tests pass a zero-delay recorder.
  - `max_iterations` bound accounts for `infra_retry_limit` so the loop still
    always terminates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `--infra-retry-limit` is present in `implement.py drive --help` and in the
   usage block; the default is `5`; a non-positive value is clamped to `1`.
2. An infrastructure refusal increments `infra_retries[child]` and leaves
   `finish_attempts` without an entry for that child (test asserts both).
3. Scripted harness returning three infrastructure refusals then success ends
   with `success: true`, the child recorded as `finished`,
   `infra_retries[child] == 3`, `infra_retry_limit == 5`, and
   `finish_attempts` empty for that child.
4. Each infrastructure retry emits a `children_driven` entry with
   `result: "infra-retry"` carrying `step`, `reason` and the attempt number,
   and spawns **no** session (`sessions_spawned` unchanged).
5. Exhausting `--infra-retry-limit` does not retry unboundedly: the loop falls
   through to the existing reconcile/reset path and stops with a message naming
   the failing `step` and `reason`.
6. The backoff schedule is bounded and injectable: a unit test asserts
   `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30]` seconds for attempts 1–6 and that no test sleeps.
7. `max_iterations` includes the infrastructure budget, and a
   always-refusing harness terminates (test in the regression item asserts the
   exact `parent` invocation count).
8. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
9. **Parent AC2 traceability.** **Infrastructure refusals do not consume the finish-attempt budget.** They are bounded separately by a new `--infra-retry-limit` (default `5`) with a bounded backoff between attempts; a refusal that clears within that budget lets the same `finish` succeed and the chain continue. Test: a scripted harness returning N infrastructure refusals then success ends with `success: true` and the child `finished`, and `finish_attempts` does **not** count the infrastructure attempts (`infra_retries` does). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the scripted-harness test first (3 infra refusals → success) against
   the extended harness from the test-harness item; it must fail.
2. Add `--infra-retry-limit` and `infra_retry_limit` plumbing plus report keys.
3. Branch on `finish_failure["kind"]` before the `finish_attempts` increment;
   emit `infra-retry`, record the delay, `continue`.
4. Add `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` and the injectable delay hook.
5. Extend `max_iterations`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` finish-failure branch
  (~8940–9100), `_drive_infra_backoff_delay` (new), `_emit_phase_report`
  (~8270), argparse block (~9630), usage block (~42).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — infra-retry budget tests.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — CLI-flag and loop-bound coverage.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Over-eager infrastructure classification hides a real gate failure.**
  *Mitigation:* explicit allow-list only (classifier item); `unknown` is never
  infrastructure; the budget is small and bounded; the chain still stops with
  the real reason.
- **Repeated retries re-run the changed-scope suite on a contended host.**
  *Mitigation:* default bound 5, exponential backoff capped at 30 s, no extra
  session spawn.

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading` — supplies
  `finish_failure` / `classify_finish_failure`.
- `Test harness: refusal scripting and commit-carrying worktree` — supplies the
  scripted `finish_failure` reports and the zero-delay recorder.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC2 (primary) and AC6 (the loop bound accounts for the new budget).

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be

- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code
  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

data.description:
## Goal

As the owner of an already-committed child slice, I want drive to never
`reset --hard` a worktree that carries commits — parking the tip on a named
`refs/wip/<child-id>` instead — so my work cannot be discarded (parent AC3).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_reset_child_worktree(worktree_path, parent_branch=..., child_id="")`
    gains a **pre-destructive preservation gate** that runs after the existing
    isolation gates (linked-worktree check, `--show-toplevel` match) and
    **before** any `git reset --hard` / `git clean -fd`:
    - compute `git -C <wt> rev-list --count <parent_branch>..HEAD` (fall back
      to `merge-base --is-ancestor <parent_branch> HEAD`);
    - when the worktree is ahead of the parent branch: create
      `refs/wip/<child-id>` at `HEAD` with `git update-ref`, then return
      `{"success": False, "reset": False, "preserved_ref": "refs/wip/<child-id>",
      "preserved_commit": <tip>, "reason": …}` — no destructive command runs.
  - `phase_drive`: on a refused reset carrying `preserved_ref`, record
    `report["preserved_refs"]` (list of `{id, ref, commit}`), comment the ref +
    commit on the child, and stop the chain naming the real step/reason. No
    session is spawned for that child.
  - `_emit_phase_report` prints `preserved_refs` in the human summary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a worktree whose `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch,
   `_reset_child_worktree` returns `success: False`, `reset: False`,
   `preserved_ref == "refs/wip/<child-id>"` and `preserved_commit` equal to the
   worktree tip; neither `git reset --hard` nor `git clean -fd` ran.
2. `git rev-parse refs/wip/<child-id>` resolves to the tip after the refused
   reset, the original commit is still reachable from the worktree branch, and
   the ref does **not** appear in `git branch` output or `git worktree list`.
3. The preservation ref is created **before** any destructive command: a
   refused reset leaves the ref in place and the worktree byte-identical.
4. A worktree that is only uncommitted-dirty (no commits ahead) still takes the
   existing reset path and succeeds — behaviour unchanged, and the reset still
   uses `git clean -fd` **without** `-x` (ignored files such as the
   `node_modules` symlink survive; test asserts the flag).
5. `phase_drive` reports `preserved_refs` for the refused child, comments the
   `wip/<id>` ref and commit hash on the child, spawns no session for it, and
   the chain-stop message names the failing `finish` step and reason.
6. The existing isolation gates (main-checkout refusal, missing worktree,
   `--show-toplevel` mismatch) are unchanged and still covered by their current
   tests.
7. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
8. **Parent AC3 traceability.** **A worktree carrying commits is never reset.** `_reset_child_worktree` refuses when the child worktree's `HEAD` is ahead of the parent branch; the tip is preserved on `refs/wip/<child-id>` **before** any destructive git command, and the ref + commit hash are reported in the drive report and commented on the child. Test: a real in-repo git worktree fixture proves (a) ahead-of-parent → no reset, `wip/<id>` resolves to the tip, original commit still reachable from the worktree branch; (b) only-uncommitted-dirty → existing reset still happens. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the ahead-of-parent refusal test and the uncommitted-only regression
   test first (they must fail), using the `commit_carrying_worktree` fixture.
2. Add the preservation gate between the isolation gates and the reset.
3. Thread `child_id` into `_reset_child_worktree` from `phase_drive`.
4. Record `preserved_refs`, comment on the child, extend `_emit_phase_report`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_reset_child_worktree` (~8148),
  `phase_drive` reset path (~9028–9095), `_emit_phase_report` (~8270).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestNonTerminalResetForRetry`
  (~646) extended with preservation cases.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — WIP-preservation ref (completed in
  the docs item).

## Risks & mitigations

- **Stale `wip/<id>` refs accumulate.** *Mitigation:* created only when a
  commit would otherwise be discarded; named in the report and the child
  comment; cleanup documented in the skill reference (docs item).
- **A ref name colliding with a real branch.** *Mitigation:* `refs/wip/<id>` is
  a fully qualified ref outside `refs/heads/`, so it never appears in `git
  branch` or worktree discovery.

## Dependencies

- `Test harness: refusal scripting and commit-carrying worktree` — supplies the
  ahead-of-parent fixture and the destructive-command recorder.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC3 (primary); establishes the no-commits-ahead invariant that
AC4's reset-for-retry slice documents.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.

  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

data.description:
## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want `reset-for-retry` to apply only
to a worktree that holds **no** commits, and its audit comment to name exactly
what was discarded (a file list, never a commit hash), so a retained commit is
never implied to have been thrown away and an uncommitted discard is fully
documented (parent AC4).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `phase_drive`: the `reset-for-retry` path is only reachable when
    `_reset_child_worktree` succeeded, which (after the preservation-gate item)
    implies the worktree carried no commits ahead of the parent branch. Pin that
    invariant in the code with an explicit guard/assert and in a test.
  - `_reset_for_retry_comment`: build the "discarded" section from the actual
    removed paths (`git clean -fd` output and/or `git status --porcelain=v1`
    captured before the reset), list them as a file list, and state explicitly
    that no commit was discarded. The comment must contain **no** commit hash
    token.
  - `_reset_child_worktree`: return the pre-reset `status --porcelain` paths in
    the result (`discarded_paths`) so the comment is evidence-based rather than
    inferred from `clean` stdout alone.
- Interpretation note to record on the parent: the parent item's "re-queue a
  finish-only retry rather than a session reset" is satisfied by the
  infrastructure-retry path (an infra refusal re-runs `parent` → `finish`
  against the preserved commit without spawning a session); a **gate** failure
  on a commit-carrying worktree stops the chain, because a finish-only retry
  would contradict parent AC6 (one attempt at the default bound).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A commit-carrying worktree whose `finish` exhausts the gate bound produces
   no `reset-for-retry` entry in `children_driven`, spawns no session, and
   reports `preserved_refs` for that child (test asserts all three).
2. `_reset_for_retry_comment` lists the discarded paths individually (one per
   line or a comma-separated list) derived from the pre-reset `git status
   --porcelain` / `git clean` output, and the comment body matches no 7–40
   character hex token that could be read as a commit hash (test asserts
   against a regex and against the preserved commit hash value).
3. When the worktree held no commits, the comment explicitly states that no
   commit was discarded, and its discarded-file list matches the files the
   reset actually removed (fixture comparison).
4. An infrastructure refusal on a commit-carrying worktree re-runs `parent`
   (finish-only, `sessions_spawned` unchanged) and never resets the worktree —
   pinned by a test.
5. Existing reset-for-retry behaviour for an uncommitted-dirty worktree is
   unchanged: reset succeeds, the child returns to `open`, and the loop
   continues with a fresh session.
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC4 traceability.** **Reset-for-retry remains only for uncommitted WIP.** The retained reset path is unchanged when the worktree holds no commits, and its comment names exactly what was discarded (file list only — never a commit hash). Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the comment-content tests first (no hex token, explicit
   no-commit-discarded statement, file list matches the fixture's discarded
   files).
2. Capture pre-reset `status --porcelain` in `_reset_child_worktree` and return
   `discarded_paths`.
3. Rebuild `_reset_for_retry_comment` around `discarded_paths`.
4. Add the explicit invariant guard on the reset-for-retry path.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_reset_for_retry_comment` (~8241),
  `_reset_child_worktree` (~8148), `phase_drive` reset path (~9028–9095).
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — `TestNonTerminalResetForRetry`
  (~646), comment-content assertions.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Comment regression (file list vs commit hash).** *Mitigation:* the test
  asserts the absence of any hash-shaped token, so a later edit that leaks a
  commit hash fails loudly.

## Dependencies

- `Commit-preservation gate before any reset` — establishes the
  no-commits-ahead invariant this item documents and pins.
- `Infra-retry budget for transient finish refusals` — supplies the
  finish-only retry path asserted in AC4.

## Parent AC coverage

Parent AC4 (primary), with the AC3 invariant it depends on.

## Notes

- **Canonical source.** Code and docs live in `~/projects/SorraAgents`
  (`skill/implement/…`, `tests/…`, `docs/dev/…`); implementation runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree for this work item's id. The installed
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` tree is a runtime copy and must **not** be
  edited — run `scripts/install_pi.sh` after landing.
- **Work-item location.** This work item lives in the `llm-manager` worklog
  (where the incident's epic `LP-0MVRO3AHN002UM1Q` is tracked) while the code
  lives in SorraAgents — the same cross-repo pattern as `LP-0MVSB0E7W003IMH4`.

data.description:
## Goal

As a producer triaging a stalled drive, I want every drive verdict message and
child comment to name the failing `finish` step and reason — plus the
main-checkout lock holder and/or the offending paths and competing work item
when the report carries them — instead of the generic
`Failed to finish child <id>`, so I can tell an infrastructure refusal from a
genuine gate failure without excavating subprocess stdout (parent AC5).

## Scope

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - Add `_describe_finish_failure(finish_failure)` → `"<step>: <reason>"`
    plus optional `"; lock held by <holder>"` and
    `"; offending paths: <paths>; competing work item <id> (pid <n>)"`.
  - Use it in every drive verdict:
    - `infra-retry` (report message + `children_driven` entry + child comment),
    - `reset-for-retry` (report message + child comment),
    - `terminal-reconciled` (report message + child comment),
    - chain-stop / `failed_child` messages (bound exhausted, reset refused,
      reset-then-fail-again, status-reset failure).
  - Read the evidence from the threaded `finish_failure` payload:
    `steps.main_checkout_lock.holder`, `steps.main_checkout_guard.offending`,
    and `_main_checkout_actor_evidence` (competing work item + pid).
  - `_emit_phase_report` human summary prints the same evidence.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the message-shape sentence in the drive recovery
  section (full rewrite in the docs item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the four drive verdicts (`infra-retry`, `reset-for-retry`,
   `terminal-reconciled`, chain-stop) produces a message containing
   `"<step>: <reason>"` (e.g. `local_dev_fast_forward: local_dev_diverged`);
   a test asserts the substring for each verdict.
2. When the finish report carries `steps.main_checkout_lock.holder`, the
   message names the holder; when `steps.main_checkout_guard` carries offending
   paths and actor evidence, the message names the offending paths and the
   competing work item/pid (tests assert each).
3. The generic `Failed to finish child <id>` never appears alone in a drive
   message when a classified `finish_failure` is available (test asserts the
   generic text is absent or suffixed with the evidence).
4. The child comments for `reset-for-retry`, `terminal-reconciled`,
   `infra-retry` and chain-stop carry the same step/reason evidence (tests
   assert the comment bodies).
5. `_emit_phase_report`'s human output prints the evidence for the failing
   child (test asserts the rendered text).
6. Changed-scope test gate green via the test skill.
7. **Parent AC5 traceability.** **The real step and reason are surfaced.** Drive's `reset-for-retry`, `terminal-reconciled`, `infra-retry` and chain-stop messages name the failing `finish` step and reason (plus the main-checkout lock holder and/or offending paths and competing work item when the report carries them), instead of the generic `Failed to finish child <id>`. Test: report/comment assertions for each verdict. Satisfied when the preceding criteria on this item pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write one assertion per verdict first (they must fail on the generic text).
2. Add `_describe_finish_failure` and thread it through the four verdicts.
3. Extend `_emit_phase_report`.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` verdict branches
  (~8940–9130), `_reset_for_retry_comment` (~8241), `_emit_phase_report`
  (~8270), `_main_checkout_actor_evidence`, `_main_checkout_guard_message`.
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — reporting assertions.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — drive recovery message shape.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Message bloat / noisy reports.** *Mitigation:* one shared formatter, one
  line per verdict, evidence appended only when present in the report.
- **Prose parsing re-enters through the back door.** *Mitigation:* every field
  comes from the structured `finish_failure` payload, never from
  `report["message"]`.

## Dependencies

- `Classifier: finish refusal vocabulary and threading` — supplies
  `finish_failure`.
- `Infra-retry budget for transient finish refusals` — supplies the
  `infra-retry` verdict.
- `Reset-for-retry limited to uncommitted WIP` — supplies the final
  reset-for-retry comment shape.

Parent AC5 (primary).

data.description:
## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the no-regression and termination properties of the
refusal-aware drive pinned by tests, so a genuine gate failure still stops the
chain at `--finish-attempt-limit` with no infrastructure retry, a
commit-carrying worktree is never reset, and drive always terminates (parent
AC6).

## Scope

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new `TestGateFailureRegression`
  and `TestDriveTermination`.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — CLI-flag default and loop-bound assertions
  for `--infra-retry-limit`.
- No production changes expected; if a test exposes a real defect, fix it in
  the owning slice rather than here (and record that on this item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `tests: tests_failed` finish failure (classified `gate`) at the default
   `--finish-attempt-limit` yields exactly one `finish` attempt, an empty
   `infra_retries`, no reset of a commit-carrying worktree, and a stop message
   naming `tests: tests_failed`.
2. A worktree-placement-violation finish failure likewise stops with no
   infrastructure retry and a stop message naming the failing step.
3. An unlisted `(step, reason)` pair (`unknown`) counts against the gate bound
   (`finish_attempts` increments, `infra_retries` stays empty).
4. Termination: with `--infra-retry-limit 5` and `--finish-attempt-limit 1`, an
   always-infrastructure-refusing harness terminates — the recorded `parent`
   invocation count equals `infra_retry_limit + finish_attempt_limit`

   `failed_child` is set, and no session was spawned.
5. Termination under mixed failure kinds: alternating gate and infrastructure
   failures also terminate within the combined bound.

Test: scripted gate-failure harness asserts one attempt at the default bound, no reset of a commit-carrying worktree, and a stop message naming the failing step. # local_active_queries leaks ~1 increment per 2.6 local requests (136 self-heals in 13 h) — capacity signal under-reports free slots

## Problem statement

The proxy's `local_active_queries` counter drifts **upward** and is repaired by the
self-healing clamp in `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries`
(`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:5718`), which logs
`local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from N to M (M active dispatch records)`
at WARNING on every repair tick (10 s). That clamp is the documented safety net from
**LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — *"False 'saturated' capacity signal starves
herdr downtime dispatcher overnight"* — plus the earlier leak fixes
LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC, LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W and LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN.

The leak is still occurring, at a high rate, on 2026-10-31:

- **136 recovery warnings** between 00:00 and 13:05 (`proxy.log-2026-10-31_00` 18,
  `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` 60, `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` 52, `proxy.log` 6).
- Delta distribution: 47× `2→1`, 18× `1→0`, 13× `3→2`, 8× `3→1`/`4→2`/`2→0`
  — i.e. almost always **one increment that was never decremented**.
- Context: **359 local streams** in the same period ⇒ roughly **one leaked increment per
  2.6 local requests** (not a rare race).

## Why it matters (impact chain)

`local_active_queries` is the proxy's in-flight local-request count. It is consumed by:

1. **`/llama/local/status`** — `available_slots`, `capacity_hint`, `active_query`. The
   herdr downtime worker's dispatch gate reads exactly these fields
   (`DOWNTIME_*_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`); an over-count reports `freeSlots: 0` and starves
   dispatch — the LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM symptom, which is why that item existed.
2. **Admission pricing** (`prefill_eta` occupancy) and the admission guard's
   `eta_occupancy_s` / `projected_wait_s`, so an over-count turns an admissible request
   into `eta_exceeds_budget`.
3. **Prefill saturation gating** (`prefill_gate_wait_ms`, `saturation=...`).

Observed in the same window as the parent finding: `12:42:45` and `12:42:55`
`WARNING local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 3 to 2 (2 active dispatch
records)` while the pool has **2 slots** — the counter claimed three in-flight local
requests on a two-slot server, so admission and any slot reader saw a server that was
busy when it was not.

## Suspected coupling (verify, do not assume)

The measured-cache-deficit abort / eviction machinery is new since
LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR ("0 pre-change" for that class) and it releases leases and records
abandoned slots on a path that also ends the request
(`lease_released`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `local_eviction … reason=…`). A skipped
`_decrement_local_active_queries` on any of those early-exit paths would produce exactly
this pattern (one leaked increment per aborted request). LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ changes the
same paths, so this must be diagnosed rather than guessed: the item may turn into an AC
there instead of a separate fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Quantify**: a deterministic analysis over ≥24 h of proxy logs reports the
      recovery-warning count, the delta distribution, and the leak ratio per local stream
      (baseline: 136 warnings / 359 local streams for 2026-10-31 00:00–13:05, deltas 1
      dominant). Recorded as a comment on this item.
- [ ] AC2 — **Locate the leaking path(s)**: identify every early-exit path that ends a
      local request (normal completion, client cancel, deficit abort, eviction,
      no-progress watchdog, tenancy-lease reclaim, slot-assignment free, exception) and
      state for each whether it decrements the counter. Deliver as a table in a comment,
      with `file:line` for each release path.
- [ ] AC3 — **Fix**: every release path decrements exactly once (or the increment is
      moved so it cannot leak). A regression test drives each path and asserts the counter
      returns to its pre-request value — including the deficit-abort/eviction paths.
- [ ] AC4 — **Invariant test**: a concurrency test (≥3 parallel local streams, mixed
      success/abort/cancel) asserts the counter equals the number of active dispatch
      records at every step, so the recovery clamp never fires (assert zero
      `counter recovered` log lines).
- [ ] AC5 — **Observability**: keep the recovery WARNING (it is the detector) and add the
      leaking request's identifying fields (`session`, `turn`, dispatch-record id, release
      reason) to it when known, so a recurrence is diagnosable without a new investigation.
- [ ] AC6 — **Target**: over a ≥60 min post-fix window with real traffic, **0** recovery
      warnings; the 24 h figure recorded in AC1 must not recur. Evidence as a comment.
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not remove or weaken the self-healing clamp — it is the last line of defence and the
  detector for this class.
- No change to admission pricing or slot-count semantics beyond making the counter
  accurate.
- If AC2 shows the leak is a benign read race in the clamp (not a missed decrement), prove
  it with evidence and downgrade the warning to debug with a documented rationale — either
  way the signal must end up actionable, not permanently noisy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_increment_local_active_queries` (~2926),
  `_decrement_local_active_queries`, `_recover_stuck_local_active_queries` (~5718),
  `_count_active_local_dispatch_records`.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` / the release paths (~1418, ~1586).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — eviction/lease-release and abort early-exits
  (`local_eviction`, `abandoned_slot_recorded`, `lease_released`).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `/llama/local/status` payload.
- `proxy/tests/` — new regression + concurrency tests.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-31)

- Clamp present with `local_active_queries > active_count` comparison; logs at WARNING.
- 136 warnings / 359 local streams in 13 h; deltas almost always 1.
- Prior related (all completed): LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM, LP-0MRIL2L3E0080OGC,
  LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W, LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN, LP-0MSAO0ZM4000QH3O.
- `wl search local_active_queries` → no open item covers the recurrence.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ** (critical) — deficit-abort 503 quarantines the whole
  `local-qwen3` entry; shares the eviction/abort release paths where this leak may live.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** (high, completed) — the false-saturated signal + this clamp.
- **LP-0MVV9JWL9003A6XR** — eviction triage for the new `measured_cache_deficit` class.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — double decrement.** Tightening one path can double-release elsewhere; the
  AC4 invariant test must cover mixed paths, not just the fixed one.
- **Assumption.** The clamp's `active_count` (dispatch records) is the correct ground
  truth. If records are themselves created late, the clamp can undercount and reset a
  genuinely busy counter — AC2 must confirm the record/counter ordering explicitly.

## Review update (2026-10-31, independent proxy-log review — session `herdr-1793450762-1330301-22426`)

### AC1 baseline correction (measured, reproducible)

Recount over every timestamped 2026-10-31 log file
(`proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749`, `_004152`, `_00`, `_06`, live `proxy.log`; 00:00 → 13:14):

| file | `local_active_queries counter recovered` |
|---|---|
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_003749` (00:00–00:37) | 2 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_004152` (00:37–00:41) | 0 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_00` (00:41–06:41) | 37 |
| `proxy.log.2026-10-31_06` (06:42–12:41) | 32 |
| `proxy.log` (12:42–13:14) | 5 |
| **total** | **76** |

- **76 recoveries in 13.2 h**, not 136 — the item's figure appears to include the
  previous-day file (`proxy.log-2026-10-31_00` spans 23:10–00:00, 13 more) and/or to
  double-count. Local streams finished in the same window: **355** ⇒ leak ratio **1 per
  4.7 local streams** (not 1 per 2.6). The defect is real and unchanged in kind; only the
  AC1/AC6 numbers need correcting so the post-fix target is measured against the right
  baseline.
- Delta distribution confirmed: **37× `2→1`**, 18× `1→0`, 11× `3→2`, 6× `3→1`, 3× `4→2`,
  1× `2→0` — i.e. essentially always a single un-decremented increment, as the item says.

### AC2 evidence: the leaking population is the abort/eviction path

For each of the 76 recoveries, the last 30 s of log was scanned for release-path signals:

| signal in the preceding 30 s | recoveries | share |
|---|---|---|
| `routing_skip_local` (any reason) | 57 | 75 % |
| local `Stream finished` | 46 | 61 % |
| **`measured_cache_abort`** | **29** | **38 %** |
| `lease_released` | 27 | 36 % |
| **`local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance`** | **27 / 23** | **36 % / 30 %** |
| `client_disconnect` | 14 | 18 % |
| `slot_save failed … ReadTimeout` | 10 | 13 % |
| `abandoned_slot_recorded` | 9 | 12 % |
| no signal at all | 9 | 12 % |

The dominant antecedent is the **deficit-abort / eviction release path** — the same lines
LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ rewrites for AC1/AC4. `client_disconnect` (18 %) and `ReadTimeout`
(13 %) are second-order candidates; the 12 % with no signal need dispatch-record ids
(AC5) to attribute.

### Additional acceptance criterion

- [ ] **AC8 — fold-or-prove against LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ, decided before either fix
      lands.** AC2's table must state, per path, whether the missing decrement is on a
      path that LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ already modifies (deficit abort, eviction after
      acceptance, abandoned-slot release). If it is, implement the decrement inside that
      item (its AC1/AC4/AC8 tests must then also assert the counter invariant) and close
      this item as a duplicate with the evidence; if not, keep this item and add the
      offending path to its AC3 regression matrix. Either outcome is recorded on **both**
      items — the one thing not permitted is two independent edits to the same release
      lines (see this item's "double decrement" risk).

## Goal

As the operator, I want an aborted local slot to stop reading as `abandoned_busy` once the abort's upstream cancel is confirmed, so that `/llama/local/status` and `capacity_hint` reflect real capacity within seconds instead of claiming the slot is consumed for 900 s.

Parent: LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ (AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

Parent criteria traced by this item (verbatim, so the automated AC-coverage review can match them):
- AC4 — an aborted slot is not "busy" for 900 s. `local_abandoned_slots` does not treat a deficit-aborted slot as busy for the full 900 s TTL — either the marker is released on the abort's own release path or its TTL is shortened for this reason; asserted by a test and observable in `/llama/local/status`.


- [ ] **AC4 — no 900 s ghost.** After a deficit abort whose upstream cancel is confirmed, `local_abandoned_slots` no longer counts that slot and `capacity_hint` leaves `abandoned_busy` — either by releasing the entry on the abort's own release path (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` / `_release_unserved_dispatch`) or by a reason-scoped shortened TTL for `measured_cache_deficit`. The chosen option is recorded in the item comment and the commit note.
- [ ] **AC4b — the annotation is NOT removed.** The `abandoned_busy` vocabulary and per-slot `abandoned` / `abandonment_reason` / `abandoned_session_id` / `abandoned_at_seconds_ago` fields keep their meaning; a cancelled-but-still-draining slot stays annotated (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM) — release only once the slot is genuinely free. `slots_detail` / stale semantics untouched.
- [ ] **AC4c — test.** A test drives the deficit abort, asserts the marker is released (or expires within the short TTL) and that `/llama/local/status` reflects it, plus a sibling assertion that a still-draining/unknown-release slot remains annotated. Existing `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`, `test_llama_local_status.py` and the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM child suites stay green.
- [ ] **AC7 — suite.** Changed-scope tests run via `/skill:test`; the item is not pushed unless the full suite is green at the dev gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a reason-aware release (`_release_abandoned_slot(slot_id, endpoint=…, reason=…)` or an explicit `release_reason`-keyed path in `_release_unserved_dispatch`) that pops the registry entry only after the upstream stream was cancelled successfully.
- Call it from `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` (which already receives `abandoned_slot_id` and `upstream_stream_cm`) once `_release_unserved_dispatch` reports the cancel confirmed; if confirmation is not observable, fall back to a reason-scoped `ttl` (for example 60 s) passed to `_record_abandoned_slot`.
- Keep `DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS` (900 s) for every other reason; document the deficit-specific value in the docstring/comment beside it.
- No change to `/llama/local/status` payload shape for this AC (the existing `local_abandoned_slots` / `capacity_hint` must simply become truthful).

## Constraints

- Do not regress LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM (draining slot never reported `idle` or `saturated`) nor LP-0MVUVHAQP001IRKK (identity recording) / LP-0MVUVHAFR0018V21 (reason attribution).
- Do not rely on a post-free session lookup; use the pinned slot identity the caller already passes.
- Depends on `[impl] Reason-scoped deferral of the deficit-marked local 503` because both edit the same abort-handler block in `proxy/proxy/router.py`; land sequentially.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC8 — red reproduction.** A test drives a local dispatch to normal completion and then advances the injected clock past the lease/watchdog horizons, asserting that today the completion is followed by `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=no_progress_watchdog` (observed 2026-10-31: served 12:43:28, evicted 12:45:55) — i.e. the test is red against current behaviour and documents the exact mechanism (`tenancy_lease_expired` → watchdog eviction → cooldown machinery).

- [ ] No production-code change in this item; the red state is recorded in a comment with the test name and the assertion that fails today.

## Minimal Implementation

- Model the harness on `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` and `proxy/tests/test_measured_cache_abort_wiring.py` (fake local stream, injected/inspectable dispatch record, monkeypatched clock).

## Constraints
