## Goal

As the operator, I want a local dispatch that has already been fully served never to be evicted afterwards, so that completed work cannot arm a local entry cooldown or look like a live aborted dispatch — the second, independent path (besides the deficit abort) that poisons the `local-qwen3` entry.

Parent: LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ (AC8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC8 — no post-completion eviction.** A dispatch that reached normal completion releases its lease/marker at completion time, so the tenancy-expiry / `no_progress_watchdog` sweep cannot reclassify it as `local_eviction_after_acceptance` minutes later. The red test from `[test] Red test: a fully served local dispatch is not evicted after completion` goes green.
- [ ] **AC8b — no cooldown from the ghost path.** Because no after-acceptance eviction occurs, no local entry cooldown and no `prefill_thrash_cooldown` window is armed for a request that succeeded.
- [ ] **AC8c — live work still guarded.** Genuine stalls (no first byte, no chunk progress, client disconnect) keep the watchdog and their eviction reasons; the existing `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` / thrash-wedge suites stay green.
- [ ] **AC7 — suite.** Changed-scope tests run via `/skill:test`; full suite must be green at the dev-push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- In the dispatch-completion path (`_cleanup_after_request` / the served-stream exit in `proxy/proxy/router.py` and its `router_helpers` helpers) mark the dispatch record terminal **before** the lease outlives the request, so the tenancy-expiry sweep (`router_helpers.py` ~5523 `tenancy_lease_expired`) and the watchdog branch (~5525–5558 `no_progress_watchdog`) see a completed record and skip the after-acceptance eviction.
- Keep the eviction-reason vocabulary intact — this is a completion-state fix, not a vocabulary change.
- Add a regression assertion in the same file the red test lives in; log a distinct, once-per-event line only if a completed record is ever seen by the sweep (cheap diagnostic, no new polling).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the watchdog for genuinely stuck dispatches; do not change `capacity_hint` semantics.
- Only the completed-dispatch path is in scope (the deficit abort path is handled by its own sibling item).

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`

## Goal

As a capacity consumer (herdr downtime dispatcher, audit runner), I want `/llama/local/status` to publish the local entry's routing availability, so that I can distinguish "engine busy" from "route armed" instead of reading `available_slots: 2` while 100 % of local attempts are refused.

Parent: LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ (AC10).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC10 — additive fields.** `/llama/local/status` gains `local_route_available: bool`, `local_route_reason: str | null` (a canonical token from `admission_reserve.LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`, e.g. `local_provider_cooldown`, `measured_cache_deficit`, `outside_available_window`) and `local_route_cooldown_remaining_s: number | null`; `status_schema_version` is bumped and every existing key keeps its name and meaning.
- [ ] **AC10b — absent-safe.** With no cooldown armed the fields read `true` / `null` / `null` (never a fabricated `0`), and the payload is still well-formed when the local entry or `llama_server_running` state is unavailable.
- [ ] **AC10c — read-only.** The proxy's own routing decision does not read these fields (no behaviour change); the values come from the existing armed-state helpers (`provider._provider_cooldown_remaining`, `_provider_failure_count`) strictly as observability.
- [ ] **AC10d — tests.** A test arms a real cooldown and asserts the payload reflects it; a second asserts the deficit abort does **not** arm the entry (post-fix) while a genuine fault does; a third asserts the idle/no-cooldown defaults. Existing `test_llama_local_status.py` assertions stay green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Build the three values in the `/llama/local/status` handler (`proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, beside `local_abandoned_slots` / `capacity_hint`), reusing the existing cooldown-remaining helper rather than duplicating arithmetic; treat unresolvable state as `None`.
- Extend the handler docstring and `status_schema_version` (4 → 5).
- Add the fields to the `status_request` log extras so the poll line carries the same evidence.
- No new polling or timers — the values are read from in-process state at request time.

## Constraints

- Additive only: a consumer that ignores the fields behaves exactly as before.
- No routing behaviour change; this is observability, not a gate.
- Depends on `[impl] Reason-scoped deferral of the deficit-marked local 503` so the tests can assert post-fix semantics (a deficit abort leaves the route available).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py`

## Goal

As the operator, I want the proxy to warn when the local route is armed for a sustained fraction of a rolling window while the engine is healthy, naming the arming reasons, so the next starvation episode is diagnosable from a single log line instead of post-hoc log archaeology.

Parent: LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ (AC11).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC11 — bounded, self-throttled warning.** At most one WARNING per 10 minutes, state-only (no new polling, no timers beyond the existing periodic sweep, or none at all if the trigger is evaluated on existing events).
- [ ] **AC11b — healthy-engine condition.** The warning fires only when the engine is healthy (`llama_server_running=true`, `available_slots > 0`) **and** the local entry has been armed for a sustained fraction of a rolling window (the measured fingerprint: 217 arms / 5.5 h, median gap 67 s, local share 2.8 %).
- [ ] **AC11c — reasons named.** The line carries per-reason counts observed in the window (canonical tokens, e.g. `local_provider_cooldown`, `measured_cache_deficit`, `prefill_thrash_cooldown`) so the cause is attributable.
- [ ] **AC11d — no false positive.** A single genuine fault in the window (one arm) does not fire it.
- [ ] **AC11e — tests.** Tested with an injected clock/state (deterministic, no sleeps): fires once for a sustained armed window with reason counts, is suppressed inside the 10-minute throttle, and stays silent for a single arm.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a small in-process tracker (rolling window of arm events with reason + timestamp, plus last-emitted timestamp) fed from the existing arm sites/observability hooks — no new polling.
- Emit via `srv.logger.warning("local_route_starved ...")` with counts; keep the message greppable and add it to the routing-docs vocabulary.
- Expose the tracker state read-only where the existing status/observability code already aggregates state (do not add status fields beyond AC10's).
- Unit-test the tracker directly plus one integration wiring test where the state feed is asserted.

## Constraints

- Observability only: no routing decision may read the tracker.
- Must not fire on startup/cold-start windows (deferral during warm-up is expected).
- Depends on the AC10 status/observability surface for engine health so both read the same state.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_route_starvation_detector.py`

## Goal

As the operator, I want measured proof that the fix moved the needle in real traffic — zero deficit-attributable `local_provider_cooldown` skips and a materially higher local share than the 2.8 % baseline — so the parent item can be closed on evidence rather than on unit tests alone.

Parent: LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ (AC9, and the AC7 full-suite evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

Parent criteria traced by this item (verbatim, so the automated AC-coverage review can match them):
- AC7 — full project test suite passes with the new changes (the existing measured-abort, thrash-cooldown, cold-start-immunity and local-quarantine suites must stay green).


- [ ] **AC9 — window and cohort.** Observations cover ≥30 minutes of live traffic after the fix with ≥3 concurrent `prefer-local` sessions (the same contention shape that produced the defect).
- [ ] **AC9 — skip count.** **0** deficit-attributable `Skipping provider=local-qwen3 … in cooldown` skips: every remaining `local_provider_cooldown` skip must be attributable to a genuine fault (a non-deferral 5xx, a post-grace connection error, or slot exhaustion), evidenced by the corresponding log lines.
- [ ] **AC9 — utilisation.** Local stream share is materially above the recorded baseline (2.8 % = 165 local vs 5 707 remote streams; 217 entry-cooldown arms / 5.5 h). The measured window's local/remote counts, arm count and median arm gap are recorded as a comparison table in a comment on this item.
- [ ] **AC9 — evidence artefacts.** Evidence produced with `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis` (and `grep` counts over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` for the exact tokens), with the fixed-commit hash and the measured window start/end named in the comment.
- [ ] **AC7 — suite evidence.** The full suite result for the fixed commit is recorded in the same comment (dev-push gate output is acceptable evidence; do not run ad-hoc full suites).

## Minimal Implementation

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want Phase A executed once, with the raw evidence
attached to the work item, so that we can state with evidence whether the
proxy actually emits a verbatim compaction marker on a real response —
settling AC1 and AC2 and producing half of the parent's AC7 verdict.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8, Phase A. Test procedure T1 (parent description)
run through the probe harness child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: T1 is executed in `--live` mode against the running proxy at a time when
  no release or audit batch is in flight; the comment records start/end
  timestamps (UTC), the probe session id, the computed trigger (expected
  88,883) and the observed `est_before`.
- AC2: Evidence is attached to this item (paths + excerpts, not `/tmp`):
  - the redacted header dump showing all four headers, with the marker body
    replaced by its length and its decoded first and last line,
  - the decoded marker's verbatim first line
    (`The conversation history before this point was compacted into the
    following summary:`) and last line (`</summary>`),
  - the matching `compaction_event … action=compact` and
    `session_compaction applied session=<probe>` lines.
- AC3: Each criterion is recorded as PASS/FAIL with its raw output: A (all four
  headers present on the compacting response), B (marker round-trips verbatim),
  C (proxy logged live application — `action=compact`,
  `reason=compacted_within_target`, `dry_run=False`).
- AC4: AC2 of the parent is recorded explicitly: the isolation check
  (`grep 'action=compact' … | grep -v <probe-session>`) output is attached, and
  if it is non-empty the failure is reported rather than papered over.
- AC5: Restoration is proven, not assumed: after the run
  `compaction_trigger_ratio` reads `0` and a post-restore probe request logs
  `reason=compaction_disabled` and carries no `X-Compaction-*` header; the
  probe session is deleted via `DELETE /admin/sessions/<id>`.
- AC6: A single verdict line is recorded on this child and on the parent:
  `Phase A verdict: PASS — wire contract verified` or
  `Phase A verdict: FAIL — <named link: config | compaction gate |
  header build | transport>`, with the failing artefact quoted.
- AC7: If the verdict is FAIL, the specific broken link is named and quoted
  (the parent's link table gets a corrected row), and the T2 execution child is
  recorded as not blocked but expected to fail for the same reason — so effort
  is not spent proving Phase B on a broken producer.
- (Parent AC1) On a dedicated probe session, one response carries `X-Compaction-Occurred: true`, `X-Compaction-Marker`, `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`, `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`, and the base64 marker decodes verbatim to the message the proxy injected (including the `The conversation history before this point was compacted into the following summary:` / `</summary>` delimiters). Test procedure T1.
- (Parent AC2) During T1 no session other than the probe session emits `compaction_event action=compact`, and the config is restored to `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` before the item is closed. Test procedure T1 steps 8–9.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py --dry-run` first and check the
  computed trigger and band; only then `--live --no-batch-in-flight`.
- Attach the harness's verdict JSON as the machine-readable record and quote
  the human summary in a comment.
- Do not hand-edit `proxy/config.yaml` outside the harness: the restore path is
  the safety mechanism, and bypassing it defeats the point of the previous
  child.

## Deliverables

- A comment on this child with the Phase A verdict, timestamps, probe session
  id and quoted evidence.
- Evidence directory committed under `docs/dev/compaction-bridge-probe-<ts>/`
  (redacted), or attached to the item when it is too large to commit.
- The parent's link table corrected if any row is disproved.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Notes / planning observations to respect

- The proxy config comment claiming `0.70 × 258,048 = 180,634` is stale; the
  real per-slot clamp is `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126,976` → trigger **88,883**
  (verified during planning). Use the computed value, not the comment.
- `summarizer_model` is `{type: local, llama_model: Qwen2.5-7B}` and the models
  endpoint currently reports Qwen2.5-7B as `unloaded` — a cold-start summariser
  can produce `reason=summarizer_failed` and **no headers**. Treat that as a
  precondition failure (AC2 of the parent's preconditions), not a Phase A FAIL;
  record it and retry after the summariser is warm.

## Dependencies

Depends on the probe harness child (T1 driver) and the proxy emission telemetry
child (criteria C/D are read from its log lines).

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want Phase B executed with bridge telemetry in place,
so that we can state with evidence whether a live pi session mirrors the
proxy's compacted view — settling AC3 and producing the second half of the
parent's AC7 verdict.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8, Phase B. Test procedure T2 (parent description).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The execution mechanism is chosen and recorded: headless multi-turn
  (`pi --print --session-id <id>`, extensions load in print mode per
  `docs/extensions.md` "Extensions load in interactive, RPC, JSON, and print
  modes") is preferred because it is repeatable; if the `context` /
  `after_provider_response` hooks demonstrably do not fire in print mode, an
  interactive operator-run session is used instead and the deviation is
  recorded with its evidence. Either way, bridge-load confirmation is recorded
  (pi log line or `/extensions` output).
- AC2: A fresh pi session on `Local Proxy/code` is driven across the computed
  trigger (88,883 estimated tokens, staying under the 120,000 warm-routing
  cap) with `compaction_trigger_ratio` re-enabled by the harness, and restored
  to `0` + reloaded at the end.
- AC3: Pass criterion D is recorded verbatim with timestamps, showing the
  ordering: proxy `compaction_event … action=compact` →
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=…` →
  `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=…` with `Y < X`.
- AC4: Pass criterion E is recorded: the next request for that session shows a
  reduced `est_before` (at/near the compacted size, **not** the pre-compaction
  value), and the next `compaction_event` — if any — is incremental
  (`turns_summarized` small relative to the session, not whole-session).
- AC5: The `history_mismatch` signal is reported honestly: `force_full_prompt`
  is `true` for **every** proxy model (`private`, `plan`, `author`, `code`;
  verified during planning), so delta routing is disabled and
  `history_mismatch` may never be logged even when the mirror works. The
  verdict therefore must state whether `history_mismatch` was observable at
  all, and must **not** treat its absence alone as proof of adoption.
- AC6: The fail signature, if present, is recorded verbatim (the parent's F4
  definition): `history_mismatch` on the following turn, `est_before` rebounding
  to the pre-compaction value, or a repeated `action=compact` whose
  `turns_summarized` equals the whole session.
- AC7: Restoration proven: `compaction_trigger_ratio` reads `0`, a
  post-restore request logs `reason=compaction_disabled`, and the bridge emits
  the passthrough line with no state created (parent AC6 evidence).
- AC8: A single verdict line is recorded on this child and on the parent:
  `Phase B verdict: PASS — option 2 viable` or
  `Phase B verdict: FAIL — <fail signature>`, with the log excerpts attached.
- (Parent AC3) A live pi session crossing the trigger shows, in order: proxy `compaction_event … action=compact` → bridge "signal captured" → bridge "reshaped N→M messages" → next proxy request carrying the compacted base with **no** `history_mismatch` and **no** from-scratch re-summarisation. Test procedure T2.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the harness's config flip/restore path rather than hand-editing config
  for the T2 run (the probe harness child owns the safe restore); drive pi as a
  separate process writing its stderr to the evidence directory.
- Move fast to the trigger by pasting a large file / repeating a long prompt
  across turns; watch `compaction_bypass_eval … est_before=<n>` in the proxy
  log to know when to stop, so the session does not blow past the 120,000 warm
  cap and route remote (which would emit no compaction at all).
- Keep the pi session id and the proxy `x-session-id` correlated in the
  comment — the whole point is to be able to line up the three log sources.

## Deliverables

- A comment on this child with the Phase B verdict, mechanism used, and quoted
  ordering/adoption evidence.
- Bridge log capture, proxy log excerpt and the pi session reference stored in
  the evidence directory.
- The parent's AC3 read against the sharper criterion (AC5 above).

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on the bridge telemetry child (the ordering evidence is its log lines)
and the T1 execution child (config safety path + a proven producer).

data.description:
## Goal

**Conditional.** If Phase A or Phase B fails because the client's rebuilt base
is not recognised as the proxy's base, implement base identity so the
divergence is detected explicitly (with a base id) instead of degrading
silently into `history_mismatch` and a from-scratch re-summarisation.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8, Phase C + AC5. **Do not implement speculatively**
— this child exists so the repair is scoped and ready, and must be closed as
"not needed" when both T1 and T2 pass.

## Gate (must be checked before any code)

- If `Phase A verdict: PASS` **and** `Phase B verdict: PASS` → close this child
  with `--reason "Not needed: Phase A and Phase B both PASS (<verdict links>);
  AC5 remains unmet by design because no divergence was observed"` and change
  no code.
- Otherwise implement exactly the failing link. Phase A fail ⇒ the producer
  contract is the defect (no base id is meaningful yet; fix the link named on
  the T1 child and re-run T1 instead of building the handshake). Phase B fail
  with a recorded fail signature ⇒ implement the handshake below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The proxy emits `X-Compaction-Base-Id` with the compaction header set:
  a stable hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex chars) of the **exact** compacted message
  list it dispatched; the same list always yields the same id and any change to
  roles, order or content changes it. The hash input/serialisation is
  documented in a docstring so the client can reproduce it.
- AC2: The proxy accepts `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` on the request. On a match it
  adopts the client's base instead of re-summarising (no CREATION
  re-summarisation) and logs
  `compaction_base adopt session=<id8> base=<id8>` at INFO.
- AC3: On a mismatch the proxy logs one WARNING naming both ids
  (`compaction_base mismatch session=<id8> proxy_base=<id8>
  client_base=<id8>`), re-signals once (emits the header set again on that
  response), and does **not** report `history_mismatch` for this cause.
- AC4: A second consecutive divergence for the same session stops mirroring for
  that session and logs the reason at WARNING
  (`compaction_base mirroring_off session=<id8> reason=second_divergence`);
  subsequent responses for that session carry no `X-Compaction-*` headers, so
  the client cannot loop.
- AC5: Clients that send no `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` behave exactly as today
  (contract preserved; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` green
  unmodified) — the handshake is additive and opt-in on the client side.
- AC6: No payload content, marker text or summary body appears in any log line
  or header beyond the existing base64 marker — only ids and counts.
- AC7: Unit tests cover: hash determinism and sensitivity (reordered turns,
  changed content, changed role); adopt-on-match (no summariser call — asserted
  with a summariser spy); single-mismatch re-signal (exactly one extra emission);
  second-divergence mirroring-off; absent-client-header passthrough; and that a
  malformed/truncated base id is treated as absent, not as a mismatch.
- AC8: The bridge (SorraAgents) sends `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` when it has captured
  a signal, and clears it when it clears state; its unit tests extend to cover
  send/clear. Recorded with the SorraAgents commit hash on this item.
- (Parent AC5) if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.

## Minimal Implementation

- Producer: compute the base id once, where the compacted list is built
  (`router_helpers.py` live-applied path), carry it on the session result
  alongside `compaction_summary_text`, and add it to
  `_build_compaction_headers`. Mismatch handling lives where the session store
  is compared (`session_manager.py` / `session.py`), reusing the existing
  `fallback_reason` plumbing rather than adding a second path.
- Client: reuse the existing per-session state map — store the id with the
  signal, add it to the outgoing header set in the dispatch path; no new
  persistence.
- Keep the "re-signal exactly once" counter in the existing per-session store,
  not in a new global.

## Deliverables

- Base-id emission + adoption/mismatch handling with unit tests.
- Bridge dispatch-header plumbing + tests.
- A paragraph in `docs/session-compaction-design.md` §7.3 describing the
  handshake and its stop condition.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`

## Dependencies

Depends on the T2 execution child (its verdict is this child's gate).

## Goal

Record and, if wanted, close the one gap the fail-closed pushed-commit guard (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9) cannot cover itself: the push that **lands** a new hook version still runs the previous hook, so a refused fast-forward on that single push can still gate a stale tree.

## Evidence (2026-10-31)

- `50167e00` (LP-0MVU94NJN008RAK0, the guard commit) was pushed after `implement.py finish` refused its fast-forward ("not a descendant of refs/remotes/origin/dev"); the main checkout still had the `v3` hook checked out, so the gate measured the stale tree and **no full-suite cache entry exists** for `50167e00`'s git state (verified by a `test_cache.compute_git_state()` key lookup).
- The very next `dev` push (`47bed454`, LP-0MVU94RN9006Z28Y) ran the `v4` hook and left full-scope exit-0 evidence at its own commit.

## Desired outcome

Decide whether to (a) leave as documented inherent behaviour (see the "Bootstrap note" in `docs/dev/git-hooks.md`), or (b) have `implement.py finish` refuse to push when its own fast-forward was skipped (framework change, SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3), which removes the trigger for every hook version, not just this one.

## Constraints

- Related/overlapping: LP-0MVRNFW0B00382D3 (non-fast-forward retry path validates the wrong tree), SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (framework: push from the worktree / name the verified tree).
- No code change needed in this repo's hook.
